Emma / Mina — technical notes to make the onboarding smooth. High-level integration checklist and example routes: 

1) SDKs & authentication
- We recommend using the Redwood JavaScript/Go SDKs for streaming integration. API key + per-route role bindings via Console.
- Token usage: enable prefix/KV caching in the SDK with default prefix length 192 tokens for RAG workflows to reduce tokens for repeated context.

2) Streaming & endpoints
- Streaming generation endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate (use chunked transfer; events prefixed with 'data:')
- Tool/function calling: include "tools" array in the request, Redwood will emit a tool_call event and then you can call your retrieval microservice via the callback. Example payloads included in attached text file.
- SDK will automatically manage KV cache across tokens for the same conversation id; for batched requests set batch_size in SDK to 8 for initial tests.

3) Performance settings (suggested start)
- Batch window: 25ms; parallelism: 4 workers per GPU; quantization: use fp16 for initial runs.
- Instrumentation: set up our token-latency tracing (trace_id header) so we can break down p95 per-token and end-to-end.

4) Acceptance checks for Week 2
- Provide an eval set (CSV of ~150 samples) that we run through both your baseline and Redwood; compare ROUGE and latency.
- Verify stable 50 RPS for 10 minutes with p95 targets.

Attachments: redwood-poc-sla-template.docx, integration-examples.txt

If you can share a tech contact and ephemeral test keys we can provide a minimal sample app (streaming + retrieval callback) within 48 hours.
